@graph.name: Cala Figuera
@graph.keywords: Fishing zone, Hard access, Rocky bottom, Deep fishing, Cliff
@graph.description: Breathtaking virgin cove surrounded by cliffs on the northernmost tip of the island, perfect for targeted fishing of large rock species.

additionalProperty.name: Access
additionalProperty.value: Access requires a 20-minute descent on foot via a rocky goat path from the Formentor road, with extremely limited parking and technical footwear being mandatory.

additionalProperty.name: Seabed
additionalProperty.value: Renowned for its rugged rocky shelves with steep drops plunging deeper than 20 meters just off the shoreline.

additionalProperty.name: Frequent Species
additionalProperty.value: Dusky grouper, Common dentex, Red scorpionfish

additionalProperty.name: Recommended Techniques
additionalProperty.value: Heavy rockfishing, Shore Jigging, Deep bottom fishing with live bait

additionalProperty.name: Time of Day
additionalProperty.value: Day, Dawn, Dusk

@graph.name: Muro Beach
@graph.keywords: Fishing zone, Easy access, Sandy bottom, Night fishing, Surfcasting
@graph.description: Extensive fine white sand beach and shallow crystal waters in Alcúdia Bay, perfect for overnight surfcasting of seabream.

additionalProperty.name: Access
additionalProperty.value: Extremely easy walk from parking lots near the protected natural area, flat terrain perfectly suited for hauling heavy gear and beach carts.

additionalProperty.name: Seabed
additionalProperty.value: Dominated by fine, light sand with a very gentle bathymetric slope. Long distance casting is required to reach depth, with sparse Posidonia patches starting past 100 meters.

additionalProperty.name: Frequent Species
additionalProperty.value: Gilt-head bream, White seabream, Dreamfish

additionalProperty.name: Recommended Techniques
additionalProperty.value: Classic surfcasting (highly preferred at night or during winter months to avoid beachgoers)

additionalProperty.name: Time of Day
additionalProperty.value: Night, Dusk

@graph.name: Cap de ses Salines
@graph.keywords: Fishing zone, Medium access, Strong currents, Mixed bottom, Foam waves
@graph.description: The southernmost tip of Mallorca, famous for its severe marine currents that draw in numerous large coastal pelagic predators.

additionalProperty.name: Access
additionalProperty.value: Arriving early is highly recommended to park near the lighthouse. Walk with extreme caution over the sharp limestone rocky coast to find the best spots.

additionalProperty.name: Seabed
additionalProperty.value: Features a shallow rocky shelf transitioning into a mixed seabed of large stone blocks and dense Posidonia meadows.

additionalProperty.name: Frequent Species
additionalProperty.value: White seabream, Gilt-head bream, Common dentex, Saddled seabream

additionalProperty.name: Recommended Techniques
additionalProperty.value: Light/medium spinning, Float fishing

additionalProperty.name: Time of Day
additionalProperty.value: Dawn, Day

@graph.name: Port of Sóller and North Coast (Tramuntana)
@graph.keywords: Fishing area, Medium access, Rocky bottom, Technical fishing, Cliffs
@graph.description: The northern coast of Mallorca, characterized by cliffs that fall directly to great depths and rocky bottoms. It is the most technical area of ​​the island, oriented towards rock species and cephalopods.

additionalProperty.name: Acceso
additionalProperty.value: Access mainly from boat. From the coast, the most productive points require descending trails in the Serra de Tramuntana, with high technical difficulty.

additionalProperty.name: Fondo Marino
additionalProperty.value: Submerged cliffs with steep drops to great depths a short distance from the shore. Rocky, coralline bottoms and underwater caves.

additionalProperty.name: Especies Frecuentes
additionalProperty.value: Grouper, Cap-roig (Escópora), Serrano

additionalProperty.name: Técnicas Recomendadas
additionalProperty.value: Bottom Fishing, Jigging, Heavy Rockfishing

additionalProperty.name: Momento del Día
additionalProperty.value: Dawn, Day

@graph.name: Bay of Alcúdia and Port de Pollença
@graph.keywords: Fishing area, Easy access, Sandy bottom, Posidonia, Surfcasting, Closed bay
@graph.description: The north of Mallorca offers closed bays with predominantly sandy bottoms and Posidonia oceanica meadows. Ideal area for fishing from the coast with surfcasting techniques.

additionalProperty.name: Acceso
additionalProperty.value: Easy access from multiple points in the bay. Spots like Sa Bassa Blanca are viable for surfcasting with good parking available.

additionalProperty.name: Fondo Marino
additionalProperty.value: Predominantly sandy bottoms with extensive meadows of Posidonia oceanica. Smooth and progressive bathymetry, ideal for long distance surfcasting.

additionalProperty.name: Especies Frecuentes
additionalProperty.value: Dorada, Sargo (Sarg), Salpa

additionalProperty.name: Técnicas Recomendadas
additionalProperty.value: Classic surfcasting, Deep fishing with natural bait

additionalProperty.name: Momento del Día
additionalProperty.value: Night, Dusk, Dawn

@graph.name: Cala Rajada and Southeast Coast
@graph.keywords: Fishing area, Medium access, Deep sea fishing, Menorca Canal, Tuna, Cliffs
@graph.description: Located at the eastern end of the island, its proximity to the Menorca channel makes it a strategic point for deep-sea and cliff fishing.

additionalProperty.name: Acceso
additionalProperty.value: From boat: access to the Menorca canal. From the coast: the cliffs offer good buoy fishing spots with access via coastal paths.

additionalProperty.name: Fondo Marino
additionalProperty.value: Mixed rock and sand bottoms on the coast. In the Menorca channel, deep waters with the presence of currents and the passage of pelagic species.

additionalProperty.name: Especies Frecuentes
additionalProperty.value: Llampuga, Dentón, Sargo (Sarg), Oblada

additionalProperty.name: Técnicas Recomendadas
additionalProperty.value: Deep sea trolling (from boat), Cliff buoy fishing, Jigging

additionalProperty.name: Momento del Día
additionalProperty.value: Dawn, Day

@graph.name: Bay of Palma and Southwest (Port d'Andratx)
@graph.keywords: Fishing area, Easy access, Dams and breakwaters, Mixed bottom, Sparids
@graph.description: Easy access area with multiple fishing spots on dams and breakwaters. Fishing is very popular in the vicinity of the port docks, always respecting the nautical signs.

additionalProperty.name: Acceso
additionalProperty.value: Very easy access from multiple urban points and seafront promenades. You must respect the signs and do not fish within the operational port facilities or in marked areas for swimming.

additionalProperty.name: Fondo Marino
additionalProperty.value: Mixed rock and sand bottoms around dikes and breakwaters, with the presence of posidonia in more remote areas.

additionalProperty.name: Especies Frecuentes
additionalProperty.value: Sargo (Sarg), Oblada, Serrano

additionalProperty.name: Técnicas Recomendadas
additionalProperty.value: Light spinning, Buoy fishing, Bottom fishing from the dam

additionalProperty.name: Momento del Día
additionalProperty.value: Day, Dusk, Night
